facts.fact_text: On 3 May 2002, the two applicants were studying at the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu.
On 3 May 2002, the two applicants attended the remembrance meeting at the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu.

According to a report drawn up by gendarmes responsible for the security of the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu, seventy to eighty 'left wing students' wearing photographs of Kenan Mak gathered in the university's canteen on 3 May 2002.
Instead of dispersing, the students displayed a banner stating 'down with fascism, Kenan Mak is immortal'.
The students chanted slogans such as 'shoulder to shoulder against fascism'.
Captain F.Y. asked the students to disperse.
Captain F.Y. warned the students that 'otherwise force would be used' to disperse them.
The gendarmes present in the vicinity used force and dispersed the students.
The two applicants and seven other students were arrested by the gendarmes.
The Bolu prosecutor accused the applicants and the remaining seven students of breaching the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).

On 6 May 2003, the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance convicted the applicants of having taken part in an illegal demonstration, on the basis of statements given by eyewitnesses, gendarmes, and video footage of the incident.

On 6 May 2003, the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance convicted the applicants of having used force when the gathering was being dispersed by the gendarmes, in breach of section 32 § 3 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
The Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance sentenced the applicants to two years and six months' imprisonment on 6 May 2003.
On 9 March 2006, the Court of Cassation upheld the judgment of the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance in respect of the applicants.

Nevertheless, the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance considered that the applicants and the other students had taken part in an unauthorised meeting and had thus acted in breach of section 32 §1 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
The Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance sentenced the applicants to one year and three months' imprisonment on 24 October 2007.
On 9 December 2002, on account of his participation in the demonstration of 3 May 2002, the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu imposed a disciplinary sanction on the first applicant Ali Akgöl.
On 9 December 2002, the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu expelled the first applicant Ali Akgöl from the university for two semesters.
On 22 August 2006, the Ministry of Education dismissed the first applicant Ali Akgöl from his post as a teacher on account of his attendance at the demonstration of 3 May 2002.

Captain F.Y. told the students that their gathering was in breach of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) because they were not holding it in the designated place, namely the canteen.

At the material time, section 10 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) required that, in order for a meeting to take place, the governor's office or authorities of the district in which the demonstration is planned must be informed, during opening hours and at least seventy-two hours prior to the meeting, by a notice containing the signature of all the members of the organising board.

Section 22 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) prohibits demonstrations and processions on public streets, in parks, places of worship and buildings in which public services are based.

Section 32 § 1 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) provides that unarmed persons taking part in an unlawful meeting or procession who, instead of dispersing of their own motion after having been warned or ordered to do so and who thus have to be forcefully dispersed by government forces, are liable to be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of between one and three years.

Captain F.Y. told the students that their gathering was in breach of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) because they were not holding it in the designated place, namely the canteen.

Section 22 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) prohibits demonstrations and processions on public streets, in parks, places of worship and buildings in which public services are based.

Section 22 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) requires that demonstrations organised in public squares must comply with security instructions and not disrupt individuals' movement or public transport.
On 2 May 2002 (the day before the meeting), the chancellor of the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu indicated his approval of the meeting taking place in the canteen of the university.
The students then proceeded from the university's canteen to the university's garden on 3 May 2002.

Captain F.Y. told the students that their gathering was in breach of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) because they were not holding it in the designated place, namely the canteen.
Instead of dispersing, the students displayed a banner stating 'down with fascism, Kenan Mak is immortal'.
The students chanted slogans such as 'shoulder to shoulder against fascism'.
The students started walking towards the chancellor's offices of the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu.
The gendarmes present in the vicinity used force and dispersed the students.
During the scuffle, Captain F.Y.'s little finger was injured by the students.
During the scuffle, a gendarme's leg was injured by the students.
In the course of the criminal proceedings, the applicants rejected the allegations of the use of force by them.
Captain F.Y. was not heard directly by the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance.

According to the judgment of 6 May 2003, in addition to Captain F.Y. and the gendarme with the injured leg, four other gendarmes had also apparently been injured by the applicants and their fellow student C.G.
In their appeals, the applicants argued that there had been insufficient evidence to warrant their conviction.
In their appeals, the applicants argued that they had not been given the opportunity to examine the video footage.

In their appeals, the applicants drew the Court of Cassation's attention to the fact that similar gatherings had been organised in the past to commemorate Kenan Mak's death and that there had never been any problems caused by those gatherings.
In their letter to the prosecutor at the Court of Cassation, the applicants pointed out that none of the injured gendarmes had accused them of inflicting their injuries.
In his application for rectification, the prosecutor noted that none of the injured gendarmes had named the applicants as the persons responsible for their injuries.
In his application for rectification, the prosecutor referred to Article 11 of the Convention.

In his application for rectification, the prosecutor argued that university grounds could not be regarded as public places within the meaning of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).

In his application for rectification, the prosecutor argued that the applicants' and their fellow students' actions could not therefore be regarded to be in breach of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).

In his application for rectification, the prosecutor argued that the students' failure to hold their meeting in a place other than the one for which permission had been granted could only be regarded as a disciplinary issue to be dealt with by the university administration and not by courts of law.
In his application for rectification, the prosecutor noted that the disturbance in the demonstration had been caused by the gendarmes' intervention.

In his application for rectification, the prosecutor noted that the reports drawn up by the gendarmes who had taken part in the operation had not made any mention of physical resistance by the students.
In his application for rectification, the prosecutor noted that the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance had not examined the video footage.
In his application for rectification, the prosecutor noted that the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance had not asked the injured gendarmes to identify the persons responsible for their injuries.

Having examined the video footage, the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance observed that eleven and a half minutes had elapsed between the beginning of the gathering and its dispersal by the gendarmes.
The Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance noted that neither the applicants nor any of the other participants in the demonstration had used force against the gendarmes.

Nevertheless, the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance considered that the applicants and the other students had taken part in an unauthorised meeting and had thus acted in breach of section 32 §1 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
According to the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance, the gathering had been unlawful because it had not been organised in the canteen but rather had taken place outside.
The sentence of one year and three months' imprisonment imposed on the applicants on 24 October 2007 was suspended.
The university's decision to expel the first applicant Ali Akgöl was not quashed by the administrative courts until 2004.
The university's decision to expel the first applicant Ali Akgöl was enforced, and the first applicant's graduation from the university was delayed for one year.
